html:
The Toraijin, "people who crossed over", were migrants from the Korean peninsula and China who settled in Japan, along with their descendants. They came in waves over a thousand years.

The early waves, from around the 300s BCE or before, brought wet rice farming, bronze and iron to the islands, starting the Yayoi period and changing the life of the Jōmon hunter-gatherers. Studies of ancient DNA show that most modern Japanese descend from both groups.

Later Toraijin came during the Kofun and Yamato period, many from the Korean kingdoms. They brought writing in Chinese characters, new pottery, silk weaving, metalwork and engineering, and helped bring Buddhism to Japan. Clans such as the Hata became powerful at court. After the kingdom of Baekje fell in 660, another wave arrived (Baekje refugees to Japan). Older Japanese histories called them kikajin, "naturalised people"; the newer name stresses that not all of them simply joined Japan.
sum: The Toraijin, "people who crossed over", were migrants from the Korean peninsula and China who settled in Japan, along with their descendants. They came in waves over a thousand years.
